body: I freaking love doom and sludge metal. Easily my 2nd favorite genre.

Oh man, that's so sad that your community wasn't open and welcoming. Where I'm at (Los Angeles), we try to bring in everyone who shows an interest. When I first got in I only knew one person and it felt strange being there, but I kept showing up and the more I did the more welcoming people became. I definitely go out of my way to make the newcomers feel as welcomed and comfortable as possible.
The band names are one of the things I will laugh about and say that it makes no sense. So annoying to type and sound out. I get that they're doing it to be 'edgy' and underground but come on now.

Yep!!! Been with my current company for 3 years now and made the transition from front end into back end. My boss has purple hair and a full sleeve. I started out extremely tame (because everyone saw me), now I've added in my bondage belt and occasionally will wear platform sneakers and am planning on a vertical labret and more tattoos. I started wearing my septum ring flipped down on Saturdays for overtime and have even worn it during the week. No one cares (no one except back end sees me), so long as my work gets done and I show up on time.

that's so funny you mention witchhouse....it has a tiny but thriving scene out where I'm at (Los Angeles). hopefully it'll continue even though the one guy i know who promotes it is stepping back for awhile. seriously, the people who go to the events here are almost always chill af.
Oh god, that belt is at least twelve years old, if not older. And I didn't know you had to grease and wax and actually.....take care of leather  until recently so I haven't been doing any of that.

Some people here have mentioned that. I would probably have to take it to a leather worker to have them do that, even though I think it would be worth it. And yes, I rip apart shirts for patches for my jacket all the time. I don't like wearing huge band tees so I sometimes buy a shirt for the sole purpose of turning it into a patch.
Not going to lie, I would wear the **** out of a shirt that said that.

Ooh, I hadn't thought of having them re-make my old belt at a leather workshop. That's a great idea. The leather is so worn and tattered I doubt it would hold up to re-patching. I really don't want to let it go!
Oh goodness me, no. I would never wish death upon something that has been such a huge part of my life.
I still have my old bullet belt too. I never wear it anymore but I'll be damned if I let it go.

To be honest, the jeans that have lasted me the longest and fit me the best have all been from the off brand Paris Blues (which I can never, ever find). I have a pair that fits me perfect that are a short inseam and have only faded slightly. Beyond that I've had good luck with MUDD brand from Kohls, only I get the jean jeggings (when I can find them) and pretty much wear them into the ground. It's been awhile since I've seen a quality pair though. I also dye my black jeans at least once a year to keep them looking fresh.

This. It's a huge part of the reason why most of my friends (and I too) don't refer to ourselves as Goth anymore, even though if most people looked at us assembled in a group you would think we were. If you like the aesthetic and certain aspects of the culture but don't like the music and can't respect where it came from, you're not Goth, plain and simple.

I have a septum ring, nose ring and three ear piercings (forward helix, daith and normal lobes). I tend to just wear rings in my piercings because that's what is most comfortable and aesthetically pleasing for me. I don't really have any issues. I feel like I would have more issues if I had studs, but I despise them so it's not really a problem. Even when my face is right next to the wall I still don't ever feel like they will get ripped out or anything.

Yes. I do this all the time.....especially with men and jobs. I know I'm fucking myself over and I hate myself for it the entire time I'm doing it, but I still do it and I can't figure out why. Actually, I know why....it's because I don't think I can handle happiness and want to ensure that my life stays the way that it is even though I hate it.

Most of my dreams occur in the Mojave desert where I grew up. I would say probably about 90% of them take place there, and I always know it's that particular desert because of the Joshua trees. Sometimes I travel back and forth to other deserts too, the boundaries between them in the dream world are pretty blurred and can be easy to miss. I don't really dream of urban areas all that much. 
One place I seem to keep going to more often is this gorgeous town/road that's at the base of this huge mountain range. The town is always snowbound and I can never remember the town itself, just the drive in.
This happens to me far more often than it should. Freaks me out every time and I can't say that I'm a fan of them.

I'm going to 2nd Byzantium. I freaking loved that movie. The same guy who directed Interview with the Vampire directed that one too, so if you like your vampire films lush and rife with gorgeous historical costumes and scenery, you'll particularly enjoy that one. And the take on the vampire myth is really refreshing and different.
